---
title: "Data Link"
output: html_notebook
---
```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(plyr)
library(tidyr)

# Configure input/output directories. Environment variables can override defaults.
# Data/ contains the neuropsychological and PET tables; the feature and final
# output directories match the feature-generation step in this repository.
data_dir <- Sys.getenv("FHS_DATA_DIR", unset = "Data")
output_dir <- Sys.getenv("FHS_OUTPUT_DIR", unset = file.path("Results", "Data"))
feature_dir <- Sys.getenv("FHS_FEATURE_INPUT_DIR", unset = output_dir)
dir.create(output_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

# Choose one feature set per run: "normal" (default) or "filtered".
# The NP/PET matching and all downstream analyses are identical for both.
feature_variant <- tolower(Sys.getenv("FHS_FEATURE_VARIANT", unset = "normal"))
if (!(feature_variant %in% c("normal", "filtered"))) {
  stop("FHS_FEATURE_VARIANT must be 'normal' or 'filtered'.")
}

input_feature_filename <- if (feature_variant == "filtered") {
  "linguistic_feature_spacy_clean_filtered_20251116.csv"
} else {
  "linguistic_feature_spacy_clean_20251116.csv"
}

output_feature_filename <- if (feature_variant == "filtered") {
  "feature_np_tau_amyloid_filtered_20251116.csv"
} else {
  "feature_np_tau_amyloid_20251116.csv"
}
```

## Prepare np test data link with feature data which generated from transcript files.
Load data from NP test, NP test complemented and feature data extracted from transcripts.
```{r}
np_test_cp<-read.csv(file.path(data_dir, "np_summary_score_neuroteam.csv"))#1534
np_test<-read.csv(file.path(data_dir, "np_test_id_idtype.csv"))#18834
feature<-read.csv(file.path(feature_dir, input_feature_filename))#655
# Preserve the original recording identifier before splitting subjectID.
feature$filename<-feature$subjectID
```
We can see that there are 1534 records in np test complemented, 18834 in np test, 655 in feature
<br>
Delete 2 dvr files, We get 653 records from transcripts.

Add id,id_idtype_date to the file
```{r}
feature<-feature%>%
  separate(subjectID,into=c('part_1','part_2','part_3','part_4','part_5','part_6'),sep = "[-_]")%>%
  mutate(
    id = part_3,
    id_idtype = paste0(part_2,'-',part_3),
    idtype = part_2,
    date = ifelse(nchar(part_4)==6,paste0('20',substr(part_4, 5, 6),substr(part_4, 1, 4)),part_4)
  )%>%
  mutate(
    date = as.Date(date,format = "%Y%m%d")
  )%>%
   select(-part_1,-part_2,-part_3,-part_4,-part_5,-part_6)
  
  
```


```{r}
# Remove two previously identified DVR recordings (row indices in the original input).
# These indices depend on the original feature-table row order.
feature<-feature[-c(597,635),]#653
```
Format the date and id_idtype columns in np test complemented
```{r}
np_test_cp$id <- ifelse(nchar(np_test_cp$id) == 4, np_test_cp$id,
                        ifelse(nchar(np_test_cp$id) == 3, paste0('0', np_test_cp$id),
                               ifelse(nchar(np_test_cp$id) == 2, paste0('00', np_test_cp$id),
                                      ifelse(nchar(np_test_cp$id) == 1, paste0('000', np_test_cp$id), np_test_cp$id))))
np_test_cp$id_idtype<-paste0(np_test_cp$idtype,'-',np_test_cp$id)
np_test_cp$date<-as.Date(np_test_cp$examdate)
```

You can check the different columns use the code below
```{r}
setdiff(names(np_test), names(np_test_cp))
setdiff(names(np_test_cp),names(np_test))

np_test_cp<-np_test_cp[,!colnames(np_test_cp)%in%c('examdate','testsubj','testtype')]
```

For convenience, select id_idtype, exam date and LMd score, and filter the na rows.

```{r}
np_test_selected<-np_test[,colnames(np_test)%in%c('id_idtype','date','LMd')]#18834
np_test_cp_selected<-np_test_cp[,colnames(np_test_cp)%in%c('id_idtype','date','LMd')]#1534
feature_selected<-feature[,colnames(feature)%in%c('id_idtype','date','subjectID')]#653

np_test_selected<-na.omit(np_test_selected)#18419
np_test_cp_selected<-na.omit(np_test_cp_selected)#1488
```
After this step we get 18419 rows in np test and 1488 rows in np test complemented
<br>
Link feature with np test data, group the data use id_idtype, and date in feature table. Calculate the difference and limit the date as exact date(diff<1).
```{r}
# Match by subject ID and retain the closest NP assessment on the same date.
feature_np<-merge(feature_selected,np_test_selected,by='id_idtype')#2071
feature_np<- feature_np %>%
  dplyr::group_by(id_idtype,date.x) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(diff = abs(difftime(date.x, date.y, units = "days")))%>%
  dplyr::mutate(diff = as.numeric(diff, units = "days")) %>%
  dplyr::filter(diff == min(diff))%>%
  dplyr::filter(diff<1)#617
```
After this step we get 617 records match entirely in np test and feature data, so there are still 36 feature data don't have np test records.   
Add new columns named combined_key for data link, and compare the difference in feature and linked data to find missing records.
```{r}
feature_selected$combined_key <- paste(feature_selected$id_idtype, feature_selected$date)
feature_np$combined_key <- paste(feature_np$id_idtype, feature_np$date.x)

feature_np_key<-feature_np$combined_key
diff_keys <- setdiff(feature_selected$combined_key, feature_np$combined_key)#36
diff_rows <- feature[feature_selected$combined_key %in% diff_keys, ]

diff_rows<-diff_rows[,!colnames(diff_rows)%in%c('combined_key')]
```
Link unmatched transcripts with the complemented NP test data.
```{r}
# Attempt to recover transcripts without an exact match in the primary NP table.
feature_np_cp<-merge(diff_rows,np_test_cp_selected,by='id_idtype')#44
feature_np_cp<- feature_np_cp %>%
  dplyr::group_by(id_idtype,date.x) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(diff = abs(difftime(date.x, date.y, units = "days")))%>%
  dplyr::mutate(diff = as.numeric(diff, units = "days")) %>%
  dplyr::filter(diff == min(diff))%>%
  dplyr::filter(diff<1)#34
```
Use the same strategy as before, and we find 34 records matched to the feature data exactly(diff<1).
```{r}
feature_np_cp$combined_key<-paste(feature_np_cp$id_idtype,feature_np_cp$date.y)
feature_np_cp_key<-feature_np_cp$combined_key
setdiff(paste(diff_rows$id_idtype,diff_rows$date),paste(feature_np_cp$id_idtype,feature_np_cp$date.x))#"3-2473 2019-09-06" "3-2951 2019-06-10"
```
After comparison, we find two recordings don't appear in np test and np test complemented. "3-2473 2019-09-06" and "3-2951 2019-06-10". So ignore them.
<br>
Add combined_key column for data linking.
```{r}
feature$combined_key<-paste(feature$id_idtype,feature$date)
np_test$combined_key<-paste(np_test$id_idtype,np_test$date)
np_test_cp$combined_key<-paste(np_test_cp$id_idtype,np_test_cp$date)
```
Filter data in the whole table(all columns) using the combined_key we generated before.
```{r}
np_test_filtered<-np_test[np_test$combined_key%in%feature_np_key,]#617
np_test_cp_filtered<-np_test_cp[np_test_cp$combined_key%in%feature_np_cp_key,]#34
```
Merge feature with np test, and feature with np test complemented. Delete redundant columns.
```{r}
feature_np_whole<-merge(feature,np_test_filtered,by='combined_key')
feature_np_cp_whole<-merge(feature,np_test_cp_filtered,by='combined_key')
feature_np_whole <- dplyr::rename(feature_np_whole, 'recording_date' = date.x)
feature_np_whole <- dplyr::rename(feature_np_whole, 'nptest_date' = date.y)
feature_np_cp_whole <- dplyr::rename(feature_np_cp_whole, 'recording_date' = date.x)
feature_np_cp_whole <- dplyr::rename(feature_np_cp_whole, 'nptest_date' = date.y)

feature_np_whole<-feature_np_whole[,!colnames(feature_np_whole)%in%c('combined_key','id.x','idtype.x','idtype.y','id.y','id_idtype.y')]
featuer_np_cp_whole<-feature_np_cp_whole[,!colnames(feature_np_cp_whole)%in%c('combined_key','id.x','idtype.x','idtype.y','id.y','id_idtype.y')]
```
Merge two tables. Finally we get total 651 records, which have exact match with id, idtype and exam date from both np test and feature generated by transcript file.
```{r}
feature_np_combined <- rbind.fill(feature_np_whole, feature_np_cp_whole)
feature_np_combined<-feature_np_combined[,!colnames(feature_np_combined)%in%c('combined_key','id.x','idtype.x','idtype.y','id.y','id_idtype.y','date.y')]
names(feature_np_combined)[names(feature_np_combined) == "id_idtype.x"] <- "id_idtype"
```

```{r}
# Record whether each NP assessment came from the complemented or primary table.
feature_np_combined$FROM <- ifelse(feature_np_combined$id_idtype %in% np_test_cp_filtered$id_idtype, 'compliment','original')
```


## Prepare pet amyloid test data link with pet tau data.
Load data
```{r}
pet_tau<-read.csv(file.path(data_dir, "pet_tau_id_idtype.csv"))
pet_amyloid<-read.csv(file.path(data_dir, "pet_amyloid_id_idtype.csv"))

```

```{r}
# Categorize years of education using the original study-specific thresholds.
pet_amyloid$Educg<-ifelse(pet_amyloid$Education_b2<=5,0,
                          ifelse(pet_amyloid$Education_b2<=11,1,
                                 ifelse(pet_amyloid$Education_b2>11 & !is.na(pet_amyloid$Education_b2>11),2,3)))
```


```{r}
pet_tau_selected<-pet_tau[,colnames(pet_tau)%in%c("bi_entorhinal","bi_Amygdala","bi_inferiortemporal","bi_inferiorparietal","bi_precuneus","bi_Putamen","id_idtype","date")]
pet_amyloid_selected<-pet_amyloid[,colnames(pet_amyloid)%in%c("id_idtype","date","ADNI.petpos","sex",'age','Educg')]
```
We get 284 rows from pet amyloid data and 244 rows from pet tau data.
<br>
Merge amyloid data and pet tau data using id idtype. and filter two exam date of these data within 1 year
```{r}
# Select the closest PET visits within a strict 365-day window.
amyloid_tau<-merge(pet_amyloid_selected,pet_tau_selected,by='id_idtype')
amyloid_tau <- amyloid_tau %>%
  dplyr::group_by(id_idtype, date.x) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(diff = abs(difftime(date.x, date.y, units = "days")))%>%
  dplyr::mutate(diff = as.numeric(diff, units = "days")) %>%
  dplyr::filter(diff == min(diff))%>%
  dplyr::filter(diff<365)

```
After merge, we can find there are 234 records remained which pet tau and pet amyloid matched.

## link Pet tau data with np test
Link feature_np_combined with pet tau data
```{r}
feature_np_tau<-merge(pet_tau_selected,feature_np_combined,by='id_idtype')
feature_np_tau<-feature_np_tau%>%
  dplyr::group_by(id_idtype, date) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(diff = abs(difftime(date, recording_date, units = "days")))%>%
  dplyr::mutate(diff = as.numeric(diff, units = "days")) %>%
  dplyr::filter(diff == min(diff))%>%
  dplyr::filter(diff<365)
```
Link feature_np_combined with amyloid_tau
```{r}
feature_np_tau_amyloid<-merge(amyloid_tau,feature_np_combined,by='id_idtype')
feature_np_tau_amyloid<-feature_np_tau_amyloid%>%
  dplyr::group_by(id_idtype, date.x) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(diff = abs(difftime(date.x, recording_date, units = "days")))%>%
  dplyr::mutate(diff = as.numeric(diff, units = "days")) %>%
  dplyr::filter(diff == min(diff))%>%
  dplyr::filter(diff<365)
```

Conclusion:
feature_np_tau have 228 rows, and feature_np_tau_amyloid have 220 rows,so 8 amyloid missed.   
tau_np_cp have 243 rows, tau_np have 220 rows, and there's no differense in the group of id_idtype and date.y(np_test date) indicate np test have 243 matched rows with tau pet. 
so there are 243-228=15 rows of feature missed(in one year of pet tau)

```{r}
tau_np<-merge(pet_tau_selected,np_test_selected,by='id_idtype')
tau_np<-tau_np%>%
  dplyr::group_by(id_idtype,date.x) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(diff = abs(difftime(date.x, date.y, units = "days")))%>%
  dplyr::mutate(diff = as.numeric(diff, units = "days")) %>%
  dplyr::filter(diff == min(diff))%>%
  dplyr::filter(diff<365)
```


```{r}
tau_np_cp<-merge(pet_tau_selected,np_test_cp,by='id_idtype')
tau_np_cp<-tau_np_cp%>%
  dplyr::group_by(id_idtype,date.x) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(diff = abs(difftime(date.x, date.y, units = "days")))%>%
  dplyr::mutate(diff = as.numeric(diff, units = "days")) %>%
  dplyr::filter(diff == min(diff))%>%
  dplyr::filter(diff<365)
```

```{r}
setdiff(paste(tau_np$id_idtype,tau_np$date.y),paste(tau_np_cp$id_idtype,tau_np_cp$date.y))

```
## 243 
```{r}
tau_np_cp<-tau_np_cp[!is.na(tau_np_cp$LMd), ]
```

```{r}
tau_np_cp$merge_key <- paste(tau_np_cp$id_idtype, tau_np_cp$date.y, sep="_")
feature$merge_key <- paste(feature$id_idtype, feature$date, sep="_")
```

```{r}
# Keep all matched NP/PET rows, even when a transcript feature row is absent.
feature_np_tau <- merge(tau_np_cp, feature, by = 'merge_key', all.x = TRUE)
feature_np_tau<-feature_np_tau[,!colnames(feature_np_tau)%in%c('combined_key.y','idtype.y','id.y','id_idtype.y','diff','combined_key.x','id.x','idtype.x','merge_key','date','date.y','date.x','sex','age','educg',"X")]
```

```{r}
np_test_cp$educg<-ifelse(np_test_cp$education_b2<=5,0,
                         ifelse(np_test_cp$education_b2<=11,1,
                                ifelse(np_test_cp$education_b2>11 & !is.na(np_test_cp$education_b2),2,3)))
```

```{r}
np_test$educg<-ifelse(np_test$education_b2<=5,0,
                         ifelse(np_test$education_b2<=11,1,
                                ifelse(np_test$education_b2>11 & !is.na(np_test$education_b2),2,3)))
```


```{r}
feature_np_tau_amyloid<-merge(feature_np_tau,pet_amyloid_selected,by.x='id_idtype.x',by.y='id_idtype',all.x=TRUE)
# Fill missing demographic values from the available NP tables when unambiguous.
feature_np_tau_amyloid$educg<-ifelse(is.na(feature_np_tau_amyloid$Educg),sapply(feature_np_tau_amyloid$id_idtype, function(x) {
    unique_value <- unique(np_test[np_test$id_idtype == x, 'educg'],na.action =na.exclude)
    if (length(unique_value) == 1) unique_value else NA
  }),feature_np_tau_amyloid$Educg)

feature_np_tau_amyloid$educg<-ifelse(is.na(feature_np_tau_amyloid$educg),sapply(feature_np_tau_amyloid$id_idtype, function(x) {
    unique_value <- unique(np_test_cp[np_test_cp$id_idtype == x, 'educg'],na.action =na.exclude)
    if (length(unique_value) == 1) unique_value else NA
  }),feature_np_tau_amyloid$educg)

feature_np_tau_amyloid$Age<-ifelse(is.na(feature_np_tau_amyloid$age),sapply(feature_np_tau_amyloid$id_idtype, function(x) {
    unique_value <- unique(np_test_cp[np_test_cp$id_idtype == x, 'age'])
    if (length(unique_value) == 1) unique_value else NA
  }),feature_np_tau_amyloid$age)

feature_np_tau_amyloid$Sex<-ifelse(is.na(feature_np_tau_amyloid$sex),sapply(feature_np_tau_amyloid$id_idtype, function(x) {
    unique_value <- unique(np_test_cp[np_test_cp$id_idtype == x, 'sex'])
    if (length(unique_value) == 1) unique_value else NA
  }),feature_np_tau_amyloid$sex)

feature_np_tau_amyloid<-feature_np_tau_amyloid[,!colnames(feature_np_tau_amyloid)%in%c('Educg','age','sex')]
feature_np_tau_amyloid<-feature_np_tau_amyloid%>%
   dplyr::rename(age = Age,sex = Sex,Educg=educg)
names(feature_np_tau_amyloid)[names(feature_np_tau_amyloid) == "id_idtype.x"] <- "id_idtype"
```

```{r}
# Historical manual correction for row 14; verify row order when using new data.
feature_np_tau_amyloid[14,'Educg']<-2
```

Finally we get 239 rows of data with pet tau and LMd while 11 rows of data don't have transcript, 10 row of data don't have amyloid status.

```{r}
write.csv(feature_np_tau_amyloid, file.path(output_dir, output_feature_filename))
```
